c.tagline: Elegant Provençal town of fountains, markets, and Cézanne's light.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and found at ranks near La Rotonde and the bus station; street-hailing is uncommon, so pre-book by phone or use an app.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; 15 is the SAMU medical line and 17 the police.

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the market crowds on Cours Mirabeau and Place Richelme, and rental-car break-ins are common — leave nothing visible.

hood_desc: The medieval old town north of the Cours Mirabeau, a maze of narrow lanes, plane-tree squares, daily Provençal markets, and the Saint-Sauveur cathedral; best for first-timers who want the historic heart on their doorstep.
The elegant 17th-century district of straight streets, aristocratic hôtels particuliers, the Granet museum, and the Four Dolphins fountain; refined and quiet, ideal for art lovers.
A newer quarter around the Allées Provençales and the Grand Théâtre near the city station, with contemporary shopping, cinemas, and dining; convenient for retail and transport.
The lively university quarter east of the centre, full of students, budget eateries, and bars; suits younger travelers and those after an affordable, sociable base.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: City buses generally run from about 6:00am to 8:00pm with reduced Sunday service; late-night travel relies on taxis or ride apps.
transit.note: Small electric Diabline shuttles loop through the pedestrian old town where full-size buses can't reach.
transit.pay: Aix en Bus runs the city network; buy a single ticket (~€1.20) or a day pass from the driver or at the La Rotonde kiosk, or use the app. There is no metro or tram — buses plus the compact, walkable centre cover most needs, and regional Zou! buses link Aix to Marseille and the wider area.

transit.m: Navette airport shuttle bus to Aix Gare Routière (~30-35 min, every 30-60 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Cours Mirabeau
The city's grand tree-lined boulevard, flanked by elegant 17th-century mansions, fountains, and café terraces, epitomizing Provençal elegance.
Cathédrale Saint-Sauveur
A striking cathedral blending Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque architecture, home to a famous triptych and cloister.
Fontaine de la Rotonde
The monumental 19th-century fountain at the entrance to Cours Mirabeau, an unmissable photo stop and symbolic gateway to the city.
Atelier Cézanne
The preserved studio of painter Paul Cézanne, offering an intimate glimpse into the working world of the father of modern art.
Montagne Sainte-Victoire
The dramatic limestone mountain immortalized in dozens of Cézanne's paintings, forming a stunning natural backdrop just east of the city.
Pavillon de Vendôme
A beautiful 17th-century Baroque mansion with manicured French gardens, showcasing Aix's aristocratic architectural heritage.
Hôtel de Ville (Aix-en-Provence)
The elegant Baroque town hall anchoring a lively square, flanked by a clock tower and the old grain market, a hub of daily Provençal life.
Quartier Mazarin
An elegant 17th-century district of grand townhouses, quiet fountained squares, and narrow streets ideal for atmospheric photography.
Musée Granet
A leading fine arts museum housed in a former priory, holding works by Cézanne, Giacometti, and Picasso in a historic setting.
Thermes Sextius
Built on the site of Aix's original Roman thermal springs, this landmark marks the ancient origins of the city founded by Romans in 123 BC.

train.note: Aix has two stations: the central Gare d'Aix-en-Provence for regional TER trains, and the out-of-town Aix-en-Provence TGV station about 15 km southwest, where high-speed trains reach Paris in around 3 hours, Marseille in about 12 minutes and Lyon in about 1h15m. No international train calls at either station - for Barcelona take the daily through service from Marseille Saint-Charles or Avignon TGV, and for Italy or Switzerland change at Marseille or Lyon. A shuttle bus links the TGV station to the centre in roughly 15 minutes, so allow extra connecting time. TER and TGV fares are separate products even though both are sold on SNCF Connect.

bus.note: Long-distance and international coaches use the Gare Routiere on Avenue de l'Europe, a couple of minutes' walk from La Rotonde at the edge of the old town. Regional Zou! coaches (https://zou.maregionsud.fr/) leave every few minutes for Marseille, a 30-minute run, and serve the rest of Provence; tickets are bought on board or at the counter. International FlixBus and BlaBlaCar Bus tickets are effectively online-only and much cheaper booked ahead. Carry a passport or ID card for services crossing into Spain or Italy, as spot checks happen at the border.

ferry.note: Aix-en-Provence sits about 30 km inland and has no port of its own, so there are no ferry services from the city. The nearest passenger ferries leave from Marseille, roughly 40 minutes away by coach or TER, with sailings to Corsica, Algeria, Tunisia and Morocco.

half.name: Marseille
half.blurb: France's oldest and second-largest city, built around the historic Vieux-Port, just over half an hour away.

half.name: Gordes
half.blurb: Hilltop stone village in the Luberon ranked among the most beautiful in France, with panoramic valley views.

half.name: Arles
half.blurb: Roman-founded town on the Rhône with a well-preserved amphitheater and the streets that inspired Van Gogh's paintings.

half.name: Camargue
half.blurb: Wetland delta region known for pink flamingos, wild white horses, and black bulls roaming the marshes.
